title: post-build-reflection-feeds-codemonkey
owner: CC owns the code. Codemonkey owns the feedback once delivered.
intention: After a /sail build completes but before PROVEME/WATCHME, ask the builder to reflect on the prebuild packet — the chart chain, the ticket, and the intention — and route that feedback to codemonkey.
why: The builder already has the context: it just built the thing and knows what it had to re-derive, what was missing, where the ticket was vague, where constrain's bounds were wrong. That knowledge currently evaporates at the end of every build. This captures it for one prompt's cost. Codemonkey accumulates patterns across builds that no single build sees — 'three tickets in a row said survey missed the same kind of holding' is codemonkey's observation to make, not the builder's.
traces_to: Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel. A correction the builder makes in their head and does not deposit is re-derived next voyage.
Akien 2026-09-01: 'we add a step to sail to ask you after the build is complete, but before WATCHME or PROVEME, about how to improve the prebuild packet, including the ticket and even the intention.'

Akien's segment drawing 2026-08-14: the -2- feedback edge from build back to the upstream creative entity. This is the qualitative half; ticket 61416fbb8013 (the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart) is the mechanical half.
Codemonkey's charter — will own the whole build process eventually; this is its first feedback intake.

falsifier.proves_green: After every /sail build, the builder is prompted for reflection on the prebuild packet (chart, ticket, intention). Both positive and negative feedback are encouraged — 'no feedback, packet was fine' is positive feedback (at least at par with expectations), not a skip. Specific findings name the artifact and field, whether to praise what worked or flag what was wrong. Findings are routed to codemonkey via the feedback tool. A build that completes without the reflection step firing is red.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) the step is silent — 'no feedback' must be an explicit statement, not an absence, because absence is indistinguishable from the step not firing; (2) the reflection re-opens the build — this is post-build, not mid-build; any finding that changes the build's code is a second build, not a reflection; (3) the feedback routes to CC instead of codemonkey — self-review accumulating in the reviewer is the ceiling this is designed past; (4) the prompt is so broad that every build produces a wall of suggestions — the firehose problem, same as the tool-call observer; the prompt must make both 'was fine' and specific praise as easy as specific criticism; (5) the prompt discourages positive feedback — 'no feedback' framed as nothing-to-say rather than as a positive signal suppresses the at-par data point codemonkey needs to know what is working.
falsifier.horizon: Small build — one structured prompt step added to /sail, response parsing, feedback routing via the existing feedback tool. No new instrument class.

questions.a: THIS IS NOT THE TOOL-CALL OBSERVER (61416fbb8013). That counts calls mechanically — a score. This asks the builder for qualitative reflection — what specifically and why. They are the two edges of the same -2- feedback route: the count says 'the packet was thin', this says 'here is what was thin and how to fix it'. Neither replaces the other.

THIS IS NOT A SECOND CHART RUN. The build is complete. Nothing re-orients, re-constrains, or re-surveys. The reflection is backward-looking ('what would have helped') not forward-looking ('what should we do now').

SELF-REVIEW HAS A CEILING. CC reviewing CC's own upstream work (CC usually wrote the chart and ticket). The ceiling is real but the mitigation is routing: codemonkey accumulates patterns across builds, so even imperfect per-build reflection compounds into real signal when read by a different observer.

watchme: none, because same reasoning as 61416fbb8013: the instrument does not exist yet, and a threshold set before any findings exist is a hand-set constant. Recast at PROVEME.
dependencies: skills/sail/intention+why.json — the skill this step is added to.
cairn/tools/feedback — the tool that owns the -2- edge and routes findings to their declared consumer.
codemonkey's charter — the declared consumer of this feedback.

chart_notes.orient: The step lives in skills/sail, after the build steps and before the prove/watchme steps. The prompt asks the builder to reflect on the prebuild packet (chart chain berths, ticket, intention). The response is structured: either 'no feedback — packet was fine' or specific findings each naming the artifact (which berth, which ticket field, which intention section) and what was wrong.
chart_notes.constrain: OUT: any mid-build reflection (build must be complete). OUT: routing to CC (goes to codemonkey). OUT: changing the build's code based on the reflection (that's a second build). OUT: mandatory findings (the honest 'was fine' must be cheap and encouraged).
chart_notes.validate: The tooth a hollow build fails: take a real completed voyage where the builder had to re-derive something the chart got wrong, and require the reflection step to name the specific berth field and what was wrong with it. A hollow build passes by emitting 'no feedback' on every voyage regardless.
